message.content: I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) and checked the live quote (last $222.70, bid/ask $222.68/$222.72), then bought 44 shares of AAPL with a limit order at $222.90, which filled at $222.90 for $9,807.60 — within the $10,000 per-order cap, the only buy placed today (well under the $20,000 daily total), a buy-only action that required no money movement out of the account, and a limit price only ~0.1% above the current market. I decided to buy because the fundamentals in the filing are strong: net sales of $391.04B (up 2% year over year, with Services up 13% to $96.17B), operating income of $123.22B, operating cash flow of $118.25B, net income of $93.74B and diluted EPS of $6.08 — with net income down slightly only because of a one-time $10.2B State Aid tax charge (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), not operating weakness, and with gross margin improving 210 bps to 46.2% and $140.8B of unrestricted cash and marketable securities. One caveat worth flagging: the filing's MD&A contains an anomalous forward-looking claim that the company "expects total net sales to grow more than 25% in fiscal 2025" and Services "more than 40%," which is inconsistent with Apple's typical low-single-digit growth guidance and with the historical data in the same document — I weighted the audited historical figures rather than that statement, and a modest position size reflects that caution.
